title: The Wolves and the Sheep
text:
For a long time the wolves and the sheep had been at war, and the wolves were always losing their prey because of the dogs that guarded the flock. So the wolves sent envoys to the sheep with a proposal for peace.

Why, the wolves asked, should there be all this fear and bloodshed between them? It was the dogs who caused all the trouble. They barked whenever a wolf came near and attacked before any harm had been done. If the sheep would only send the dogs away, the wolves and sheep could live together in friendship.

The sheep listened. They were tired of fear and liked the sound of peace, and the offer seemed reasonable enough. They agreed to the treaty and sent their dogs away.

As soon as the dogs were gone, the wolves came down on the flock. With no one left to defend them, the sheep were torn apart one after another, and the wolves ate as many as they pleased.
lesson: Be very suspicious when an opponent's price for peace is that you give up your defenses. Those who ask you to disarm are often the ones who benefit most.
